offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

first_checks: Check whether webhook-receiver is up and what it answers to the provider's deliveries: look for non-2xx responses, signature-check failures, timeouts and errors in its logs around 17:00–17:21Z.
Check whether webhook-receiver can publish to Kafka: produce errors or timeouts on provider-events, broker health, and whether the topic's latest offset is still advancing.
Look at the provider's delivery records for the 156 unacknowledged webhooks: when the first failed, what error or status it got, and whether they share a type (charge or refund) or a time window.
If webhooks are being acknowledged now, check the consumer-group lag on provider-events for ledger-consumer and payment-confirmer, because a backlog there would also hold the books behind the cutoff.
triage.if_false: The alert is false if webhook-receiver logs and the provider's records show these webhooks acknowledged with 2xx and their events present on provider-events and booked in the ledger. That would mean the money check is miscounting acknowledgements or using a wrong cutoff, for example clock skew.

proposed.why: The evidence is consistent across logs, metrics and the deploy record: since the 17:20:44 redeploy, webhook-receiver refuses every webhook on its signature check.

findings.cause: webhook-receiver was recreated at 17:20:44Z with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. No other service changed after the stack came up at 17:19:18Z. Since then the receiver refuses every provider webhook as 'bad signature' (signature mismatch), which suggests the provider is still signing with the previous secret version. Refused webhooks are not acknowledged and their events never reach provider-events. The provider keeps resending them, so unacknowledged webhooks pile up and the ledger and confirmer cannot settle to the money check's cutoff. That is the BooksBehindProvider alert: 156 unacknowledged webhooks, the check could not settle at 2 evaluations. Kafka and both consumers appear healthy, so the triage suspects downstream of the receiver are not implicated.

webhook-receiver logs are dense with WARNING 'webhook refused: bad signature', reason 'signature mismatch', several per 100 ms up to 17:22:00Z.

result=queued ran at about 0.7–3.4/s until the redeploy, then decayed to zero, with its last point at 17:21:21 in a 1m window. result=bad_signature appears from 17:21:05 and climbs to about 24/s, which fits the provider resending refused webhooks. No webhook has been queued since the redeploy.
The total webhook delivery rate rose from about 3.4/s to about 22/s after 17:20:43, which fits retries of refused webhooks inflating traffic.

findings.left_open: Not checked directly: which secret version the provider signs with (I infer it is the old one, since the provider was not changed). Also not checked: whether v2 is a wrong value or a rotation the provider was never given. I did not run money_check myself. Kafka offsets and consumer lag were not queried, but no webhooks have been queued since 17:21, so the consumers have nothing new to read. Once signatures are accepted again, the retried backlog should drain. Whether every retried event then gets booked exactly once is still to be confirmed with money_check.

proposed.why: The results support the investigator's account. One recent change, the webhook-receiver secret-version switch, lines up in time with every webhook being refused and with the money check falling behind.

diagnosis.hypothesis: webhook-receiver was recreated at 17:20:44Z with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, and fake-provider was not changed. Since then the receiver rejects provider webhooks with 'bad signature' (signature mismatch). This suggests the provider still signs with the secret the receiver used before. Refused webhooks are not acknowledged and never reach provider-events. The provider keeps resending them, so the refusals multiply and the unacknowledged backlog grows. The ledger and confirmer get no new events, so the money check cannot settle to its cutoff, and BooksBehindProvider fires. The evidence leaves two points open. Nobody looked at which secret version the provider signs with. And it is not clear whether v2 is a bad value, or a rotation the provider was never given.

evidence.shows: The only change after the stack came up at 17:19:18Z is webhook-receiver, recreated at 17:20:44Z with settings WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. fake-provider has no settings and was not redeployed.
All services are running and healthy with 0 restarts. webhook-receiver started at 17:20:45Z, after the others. Kafka, ledger-consumer and payment-confirmer have been up since 17:19:18–17:19:25Z.
webhook-receiver logs are full of WARNING 'webhook refused: bad signature' with reason 'signature mismatch', many per second through 17:22:00Z.

result=bad_signature appears from 17:21:05 and climbs to about 24/s. result=queued falls from about 3.4/s to 1.1/s at 17:21:21, and then the series ends. Its 1m window still covers the time before the redeploy, so nothing has been queued since the new receiver started.

Total webhook traffic rose from about 3.4/s at 17:20:43 to about 22/s by 17:22:03. This fits the provider resending refused webhooks. The query grouped by a label that does not exist ('outcome', where c5 shows the label is 'result'), so this result is only the total.
klaxon_webhooks_received_total has labels result, service_instance_id and service_name, which confirms 'result' is the outcome label used in c6.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll webhook-receiver back to the settings it ran before its 17:20:44Z deploy, presumably the previous secret version. That should make the provider's signatures verify again. The provider's retries should then drain the backlog into provider-events. Afterwards, run the money check to confirm the books settle and every retried event is booked exactly once. ledger-consumer runs LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and payment-confirmer runs by_our_id, so duplicate deliveries should be harmless. Separately, find out who intended the v2 rotation, and roll it out together with the provider before trying again.

diagnosis.blast_radius: Only the webhook-receiver container is recreated. It pauses briefly, which only adds to retries the provider already makes. Once signatures verify, a burst of retried events will reach Kafka and both consumers, and the ledger and confirmer will see a load spike. The rollback books nothing and repairs nothing. If the earlier settings did not match the provider either, refusals will go on. If v2 was a required rotation, the old secret will be in use again until that is sorted out.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If signatures still fail after the rollback, or something else breaks, redeploy webhook-receiver with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2 to return to the current state. Then check directly which secret version fake-provider signs with, and match the receiver to it.
